newsitem.title: UK: Airtours, Carnival to buy Costa line. [CORRECTED 15:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Airtours, Carnival to buy Costa line. [CORRECTED 15:42 GMT]

text.p: British-based holiday operator Airtours Plc and its U.S. cruise partner Carnival Corp, said on Thursday they had signed a letter of intent with the main owners of Italian cruise line Costa Crociere SpA to buy the company.

The two prospective purchasers said in a statement that in due course, they expected to launch a joint tender offer, which would make them 50-50 owners of Costa, and expected to pay about 452 billion lire, or 181 million pounds ($301 million) in total.

Costa Crociere, based in Genoa, claims to be Europe's largest cruise company with 10 ships and in the year to end 1995 (Corrects from 1996) produced a profit before tax of about 18.2 million pounds on turnover of about 308 million pounds.
Under the terms of their likely bid, Airtours and Carnival expect to pay 3,875 lire per ordinary share, 2,500 lire per saving share and 285 lire per saving warrant.
"Both Airtours and Carnival intend to meet their share of the offer out of existing resources or lines of credit," the statement added.

Carnival and Airtours formed a strategic alliance in March, combining the might of the world's largest cruise line operator with one of the largest air holiday operators, and Carnival took a near 30 percent stake in the British firm. ($1=.6003 Pound)
